title: Comma colimit of a coherent covariant corepresentable
statement:
Use small quasicategories, coherent transformations, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the infinity category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ of small spaces of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Use the coherent Hom functors and their functoriality from [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$, let $K,Z$ be $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories, let $v:K\to Z$ be a coherent functor, and let $k\in K$ and $z\in Z$. Form the coherent comma quasicategory
$$I_z=K\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{Z,\operatorname{ev}_1}\{z\},$$
where the map from $K$ is $v$. Its objects are $(t,\alpha:v(t)\to z)$, with their coherent triangle data and all higher simplices, and let $p:I_z\to K$ be the projection. The coherent diagram $D:I_z\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ is $D(t,\alpha)=\operatorname{Map}_K(k,t)$. Applying $v$ and composing with the tautological arrow $\alpha$ gives a coherent cocone with apex $\operatorname{Map}_Z(v(k),z)$ and legs
$$\operatorname{Map}_K(k,t)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_Z(v(k),z),\qquad f\longmapsto\alpha\circ v(f).$$
This specified cocone is colimiting. In particular the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{(t,\alpha)\in I_z}\operatorname{Map}_K(k,t)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_Z(v(k),z)$$
is an equivalence of spaces. All functor categories and cocone categories are formed in a containing universe; the assertion concerns whole spaces and coherent cocones, not only their sets of components.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.14, last assertion and its Yoneda proof, printed pp. 269–270, applied to opposite categories; the colimit dual of Proposition 6.4.9, printed p. 298. These give the pointwise left Kan extension of a covariant corepresentable. Online July 30, 2026 revision read by the second reader; no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Let $T_z=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Z)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Z}\{z\}$. Its source projection to $Z$ is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration]. Pulling back its horn lifting problems along $v$ shows directly that $p:I_z\to K$ is a right fibration. Its total space is a quasicategory: project an inner horn to $K$, fill there, then use the right-fibration lift. The simplicial sets are $\mathcal U$-small since all their simplex data are finite-simplex maps into the small simplicial sets $K,Z$. Write $Q_p$ for the coherent contravariant fiber transport of [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit].

source.place: Proposition 6.1.14, printed pp. 269–270, Yoneda argument; mapping-out version using the right Kan formula for a right fibration from Kerodon 7.3.4.1, 7.3.4.4 and 7.3.6.1. Online sources, archival copies WANTED.

proof.text: Identify this transport with $Q(t)=\operatorname{Map}_Z(v(t),z)$, with precomposition as its arrow maps. To justify this for the entire coherent diagram, first use the join-slice right fibration $J=K\times_Z Z_{/z}\to K$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. The final clause of [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit] explicitly identifies its transport $Q_J$ with $Q$. The comparison $\delta_z:Z_{/z}\to T_z$ of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] is an equivalence of quasicategories over $Z$; both are right fibrations over $Z$, by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] and [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration]. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] each fiber map $(Z_{/z})_y\to(T_z)_y$ is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. Its pullback along $v$ is a map $\phi:J\to I_z$ of right fibrations over $K$, and the fibers of $J$ and $I_z$ over $t$ are literally the fibers of $Z_{/z}$ and $T_z$ over $v(t)$, so every fiber map $\phi_t$ is a homotopy equivalence. [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit] states that its transport construction is natural for maps of right fibrations over $K$. Hence $\phi$ induces a coherent transformation $Q_J\to Q_p$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$ whose vertex components are the maps $\phi_t$. Since these components are equivalences, the objectwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes it a coherent equivalence, and so $Q\simeq Q_J\simeq Q_p$. On fiber points $\delta_z$ sends the $1$-simplex $\alpha:\Delta^1\to Z$ with last vertex $z$ to the same arrow, so the fiber point $\alpha:v(t)\to z$ of $I_z$ corresponds to that arrow in $Q(t)$, and transport along $f:t\to t'$ is $\alpha'\mapsto\alpha'\circ v(f)$; the comparison and all its simplices respect these transports.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.14, printed pp. 269–270, Yoneda argument; mapping-out version using the right Kan formula for a right fibration from Kerodon 7.3.4.1, 7.3.4.4 and 7.3.6.1. Online sources, archival copies WANTED.

proof.text:
Put $F(t)=\operatorname{Map}_K(k,t)$, a coherent functor by [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]. Use the coherent small-space corepresentable model supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation], with its distinguished identity point; mapping-space identifications below are coherent comparison equivalences, rather than equalities of simplicial sets. For any small space $X$, [lem-coef-right-fibration-constant-right-kan] applied to $p:I_z\to K$ identifies the space of coherent cocones $Fp\to\Delta_{I_z}X$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(F,R_X)$, where $R_X(t)=\operatorname{Map}(Q_p(t),X)$. Replace $Q_p$ by the coherent equivalence $Q$ of step 2. The Hom-functor theorem and the equivalence-on-mapping-spaces clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] give the corresponding equivalence of these coherent $R_X$ diagrams. Apply the explicit covariant dual of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] to $(K,k,R_X)$. Evaluation at $1_k$ gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(I_z,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})}(D,\Delta_{I_z}X)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(Q(k),X)=\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{Map}_Z(v(k),z),X).$$
All equivalences concern whole spaces and are natural in $X$, not just component sets.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.14, printed pp. 269–270, Yoneda argument; mapping-out version using the right Kan formula for a right fibration from Kerodon 7.3.4.1, 7.3.4.4 and 7.3.6.1. Online sources, archival copies WANTED.

proof.text:
Check that the inverse of the last equivalence is induced by the specified cocone. Given $g:Q(k)\to X$, the inverse Yoneda formula of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-yoneda-evaluation] gives $\theta_t(f)=R_X(f)(g)=g\circ Q(f)$. The inverse/counit formula of [lem-coef-right-fibration-constant-right-kan] then gives, at $(t,\alpha)$, the map
$$f\longmapsto\theta_t(f)(\alpha)=g(Q(f)(\alpha))=g(\alpha\circ v(f)).$$
These formulas apply to coherent simplicial parameters by both cited statements; the precomposition and identity/composition homotopies are those of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] and [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. Consequently this equivalence is exactly postcomposition of the given cocone with $g$. The dual cocone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that this specified cocone is colimiting with apex $Q(k)$. Comparing its universal property with that of any chosen colimit makes the canonical map in the statement an equivalence. No separate assumption of existence of space colimits is needed.
